props.title: Why this list is the point
props.text: A source below is **approved**, **in the index** and **past its review date**. Nothing is broken and no alarm has fired — it is simply still answering questions on material nobody has re-checked. Open one to re-review it, or request its removal.

props.emptyText: No knowledge bases yet — add one on Setup.
Nothing is answering past its review date. That is the state this register is for.

No personal-data findings recorded. If the scan date above is empty, that means nobody has looked.

props.text: Proposing a removal marks the source **removal pending** and logs it. It is not gone from the index until somebody confirms that on the Retirements screen — which is the gap this register exists to close.

props.name: finding
props.label: What was flagged — describe it, never paste it

props.name: is_special_category
props.label: Special category (Art. 9) — beliefs, union membership, sex life, ethnicity

props.text: A finding says WHAT was found and WHERE — never the value itself, or this register becomes a second copy of the data it is meant to police. Health and biometric findings are marked Art. 9 whether or not the box is ticked. Recording one does not mean the whole source has been checked: set **Scanned** on the Sources screen once it has.

screens.description: Sources submitted or in review, waiting for a decision.

props.title: Review queue
props.subtitle: Everything a human still has to decide about. Open a source to move it up the ladder — approval is a decision, so it happens on the record, not from a row menu.

props.label: Waiting, never scanned
props.caption: approving one of these is the risk

props.label: Waiting, no legal basis
props.caption: nobody said why we may use it

props.title: Before you approve
props.text: The list on the right is everything in this queue that has **never been scanned for personal data**. Approving one of those puts unchecked material in front of every assistant that may read the base.

props.emptyText: Nothing is waiting. Every source has been decided about.
Everything in the queue has been scanned.

screens.name: Review calendar
screens.description: When each approval expires, and what already has.

props.title: Review calendar
props.subtitle: An approval is a decision about a moment in time. This is when each of them runs out.

props.label: No review date set
props.caption: these will never come up again

props.emptyText: No source has a review date yet.

screens.name: Personal data
screens.description: What a scan flagged inside a source, and the ruling on it.

props.title: Personal-data findings
props.subtitle: Decision and rationale are editable inline. A finding is never deleted — an accepted one is a decision on the record, not an absence.

props.label: Indexed, never scanned
props.caption: the gap these findings cannot describe

props.title: The scan is an automation you wire up
props.text: This app records findings; it does not detect them. **Run the scan** fires an automation which is not connected yet — point it at your PII detection service (Bee Flow ships one) in Automations, and its results land in this table. Until then, open a source and record findings by hand at the bottom of its screen; the "never scanned" number above is the honest picture, and the Scanned date is yours to set on the Sources screen.

props.emptyText: No findings recorded. That is either good news or nobody has scanned anything — the third number above tells you which.

screens.description: Which assistants, agents and groups may read which base.

props.title: Who may ask
props.subtitle: A knowledge base becomes a breach at the moment somebody is granted access to it who should not have been. Every grant here says who, why, and until when.

props.label: Expired but still active
props.caption: past their end date and never revoked

props.emptyText: No knowledge bases yet — add one on Setup.
Nobody has been granted access to this base yet.

props.name: can_export
props.label: May hand back whole documents, not just answers

screens.name: Retirements
screens.description: What was removed, why, and whether the index actually dropped it.

props.title: Retirements
props.subtitle: Deciding to remove a source and the index having dropped it are two events. Confirm the second one here.

props.label: Awaiting removal
props.caption: decided, not yet out of the index

props.title: A retired source that is still indexed is the failure this register exists to prevent
props.text: Confirming a removal here marks the log entry **removed**, and sets the source back to **not indexed** so no screen claims it is still answering. Do it only once the retrieval index has genuinely dropped the material.

props.emptyText: Nothing has been proposed for removal. Propose one from a source, or from the Register.

screens.name: Setup
screens.description: Bases, the review ladder and the legal bases you recognise.

props.title: Setup
props.subtitle: The approval ladder and the legal bases are data, not code — add a rung here and it appears as a control on every source.

props.title: Three things to know
props.text:
**Counts as** is what the app reasons in — only `live` may answer, and `closed` must not be in the index. Rename a state freely; change what it counts as and sources already in it keep their old rung until someone sets their state again.

The Stage and Legal basis dropdowns in the filter bars and the add-a-source form are fixed lists. A rung or a basis you add here shows up on every source and in every grid, but not in those dropdowns until an editor adds it there too.

A rung or a legal basis can be deleted — sources keep the key they already store, so nothing moves screens. A knowledge base cannot: its sources, grants and findings carry its name as a copy, and deleting it would leave them answering with nothing to reach them by. Untick **Active** instead.

Removal proposed. Confirm it on the Retirements screen once the index has dropped it.

Recorded, and open for a decision. Set the scan date on the Sources screen once the whole source has been checked.

then.message: Access granted, and logged against your name.

else.message: Pick the knowledge base on the left first — a grant is always to one base. If that list is empty, add a base on Setup.

Delete this legal basis? Sources that cite it keep the key and their permission note — you are removing it from the list of grounds you recognise, not from the sources.
